questions.concept: Reason HAVING was added to SQL
questions.question: Why was the HAVING clause added to SQL?

options.A: To sort query output in a chosen order
options.B: To join two tables on a shared column
options.C: WHERE cannot be used with aggregate functions
options.D: To delete duplicate rows from a grouped result table

questions.explanation: HAVING was added because the WHERE keyword cannot be used with aggregate functions such as MIN(), MAX(), SUM(), AVG() and COUNT(). It is used with GROUP BY.

questions.question: The Intel 8085 microprocessor has an address bus of what width?
questions.explanation: The 8085 (Intel, 1977) is an 8-bit CPU with an 8-bit data bus, a 16-bit address bus and 40 pins.

questions.concept: LBA as a limited-memory Turing machine
questions.question: Which machine is described as a type of Turing machine with limited memory?
questions.explanation: Linear Bounded Automata are a type of Turing machine with limited memory. Pushdown automata recognize context-free languages and finite automata recognize regular languages.

questions.concept: String immutability: assigning to str index raises TypeError
questions.question:
What happens when the following code runs?
str1 = 'Hello World!'
str1[1] = 'a'

options.C: A new string is created silently

questions.explanation: A string is immutable, so assigning a new value to a character position such as str1[1] = 'a' raises a TypeError.

questions.question: Which port number is used by IMAP?
questions.explanation: IMAP uses port 143. Port 110 is POP3, 194 is IRC and 443 is HTTPS.

questions.question: Which encryption standard is used in most ATMs?
questions.explanation: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is used in most ATMs. PGP is used for email security and WPA2 for Wi-Fi security.

questions.question: Belady's Anomaly, where increasing page frames increases page faults, is always seen in which page replacement algorithm?
questions.explanation: Belady's Anomaly occurs when more page frames lead to more page faults, and it is always seen in the FIFO page replacement algorithm.

questions.concept: Origin of the term Machine Learning
questions.question: Who coined the term Machine Learning while at IBM?
questions.explanation: Machine Learning was coined by Arthur Samuel at IBM. John McCarthy coined Artificial Intelligence, and Geoffrey Hinton is associated with Deep Learning.

questions.concept: Modifying a variable through a pointer
questions.explanation: & returns the address of x, so p points to x. The dereference operator * accesses x through p, so *p = 9 changes x to 9.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes an input-restricted dequeue?

options.A: Insertion and deletion are both allowed at only one end
options.B: Deletion at only one end, insertion at both ends
options.C: Insertion at only one end, deletion at both ends
options.D: Elements are removed strictly by their priority

questions.explanation: In an input-restricted dequeue, insertion is allowed at only one end while deletion is allowed from both ends. The reverse describes an output-restricted dequeue.

questions.concept: Adhoc testing executed without documentation and planning
questions.question: Which type of software testing is executed without any documentation and planning?
questions.explanation: Adhoc testing is executed without documentation and planning. Smoke testing validates the build and regression testing re-runs previous test cases in maintenance.

questions.question: Which of the following devices operate at the Physical Layer of the OSI model? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Hub and Repeater work at the Physical Layer. A Switch works at the Data Link Layer and a Router at the Network Layer.

questions.question: Which type of ROM can be erased and reprogrammed using UV rays?
questions.explanation: EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM) is edited using UV rays. PROM cannot be edited, and EEPROM is erased electrically.

questions.question: In e-commerce, what is a chargeback?

options.A: A processing fee charged by the payment gateway
options.B: A dispute initiated by the buyer with their bank
options.C: A discount offered at the shopping cart
options.D: A loyalty reward credited after purchase

questions.explanation: A chargeback is a dispute initiated by the buyer with their bank, which reverses the funds.

questions.question: In the textbook example, num1 = 20 and num2 = 30 - 10. What does comparing id(num1) and id(num2) show?

options.B: They differ since num2 is computed
options.C: Both ids are exactly the same
options.D: id() raises an error for integers

questions.explanation: Python treats every value as an object with a unique identity. In Example 5.2, id(num1) and id(num2) both return 1433920576 because both refer to the same object, 20.

questions.question: Free memory holes are 100 KB, 500 KB, 200 KB, 300 KB and 600 KB (in that order). Using Best Fit, which hole is allocated to a 212 KB process?
questions.explanation: Best Fit chooses the smallest free partition that can fit the process. The smallest hole of at least 212 KB is 300 KB. First Fit would pick 500 KB and Worst Fit 600 KB.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four types of AI?
questions.explanation: The four types of AI are Reactive Machines, Limited Memory, Theory of Mind and Self-aware AI. Expert Systems is a branch of AI, not a type.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a NoSQL database?
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL is an open-source object-relational (SQL) database. MongoDB, Neo4J and HBase are NoSQL databases.

questions.question: The technique of hiding information inside an image is called:
questions.explanation: Steganography hides information inside an image; the data is embedded rather than transformed into an obscure format as in encryption.

questions.question: Which command displays the possible routes of packets and measures transit delays, up to a maximum of 30 hops?
questions.explanation: Tracert (Traceroute) displays possible routes and transit delays of packets with a maximum of 30 hops, using ICMP. Ping only tests reachability.

questions.question: Which language is recognised as the first object-oriented programming language (1967)?
questions.explanation: Simula (1967) was the first OOPS language. Smalltalk is the first pure (100%) object-oriented language.

questions.concept: Null pointers in a doubly linked list
questions.question: How many null pointers does a doubly linked list contain?
questions.explanation: A doubly linked list has two null pointers. A singly linked list has one, and a circular linked list has zero.

questions.concept: Turing machine introduced by Alan Turing in 1936
questions.question: In which year did Alan Turing introduce the Turing machine?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing introduced the Turing machine in 1936.

questions.question: Which type of online advertisement are people least willing to tolerate?
questions.explanation: People are most willing to tolerate banner ads, while pop-under ads are the least tolerated.

questions.question: Which order correctly arranges memory from fastest to slowest?
questions.explanation: The memory hierarchy from fastest to slowest is Register, Cache, RAM, Hard Disk. Cache is the second fastest memory.
